comparison: Perfect agreement on C6, C22, C23. Both evaluations find the cryo-EM structure at 3.28 Å resolution and extended conformation with enclosed channel to be well-supported. OpenEval cites Figures 2 and 6; peer reviewers describe the structure as 'solid' and 'valuable information.'

Perfect agreement on C84-C90. Both accept the CryoDRGN conformational heterogeneity analysis and identification of compact forms. OpenEval notes limitations (streaking, low particle number) but validates biological relevance; peer reviewers acknowledge the computational analysis without challenging the findings, though they note the work is 'very descriptive.'

Strong agreement on C70-C79 regarding channel identification and characterization. Both accept MOLE predictions and amino acid composition analysis. OpenEval emphasizes functional relevance of lysine depletion and catalytic cysteine positioning; peer reviewers implicitly accept channel analysis when noting 'aldehyde intermediate resides longer in the channel.'

Divergent evaluations on C7, C24-C25, C80-C82, C101-C102. OpenEval finds MD simulations strongly support acetaldehyde channeling mechanism with significantly longer residence times. Peer reviewers acknowledge the MD work but emphasize it 'does not provide mechanistic understanding,' rating the evidence as UNCERTAIN rather than fully establishing mechanism.

Agreement on C37-C44 structural comparisons. Both accept buried surface area calculations and quantitative interface analysis showing extended forms have larger buried areas. OpenEval presents as standard structural metrics; peer reviewers acknowledge comparative analysis as a strength without challenge.

Agreement on C26-C28, C32-C33 regarding negative stain TEM findings. Both accept that C. thermocellum AdhE remains extended in E. coli while native E. coli AdhE is compact, demonstrating sequence-dependent conformational preferences. Peer reviewers also accept cofactor effects (C30-C31) and spirosome length analysis (C34-C35) covered in same result.

Agreement on C63-C68 regarding active site architecture. Both accept structural alignment findings, NAD+ clash observations, and water molecule identification. OpenEval emphasizes MD simulation validation (>98% occupancy); peer reviewers accept these as solid structural details without challenge.

Agreement on C57-C62 regarding GxGxxG motif identification. Both accept the novel structural feature with >99% conservation and location at monomer interface. OpenEval notes functional validation is needed for allosteric regulation; peer reviewers accept as part of solid structural characterization without explicit challenge.

Agreement on C50-C53 regarding structural comparisons with mutagenesis studies. Both accept tyrosine substitution maintaining hydrophobic pocket and linker deletion disrupting dimerization. Peer reviewers acknowledge sequence-structure correlations as part of comparative framework strength; OpenEval finds reasonable inference from structural data.

Divergent evaluations on C45-C49, C91-C92. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN because structural analysis showing more interactions in extended forms 'disagrees with reality' that E. coli compact is stable apo form, with authors unable to explain discrepancy. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for different reason: interpretations about conformational stability viewed as incomplete without mechanistic understanding.

Agreement on C30-C31 regarding cofactor-dependent conformational changes. Both accept negative stain EM findings showing metabolic regulation of spirosome structure. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with prior E. coli work; peer reviewers accept as descriptive findings without objection.

Agreement on C34-C35 regarding quantitative spirosome length measurements. Both accept statistical significance from Mann-Whitney U test. OpenEval notes parallel with V. cholerae observations; peer reviewers accept as part of comparative conformational analysis without challenge.

Partial overlap on C83. OpenEval finds cross-species conservation of channeling mechanism strengthens hypothesis. Peer reviewers acknowledge MD simulations showing longer residence times but emphasize insufficient mechanistic understanding, suggesting acceptance of observation but uncertainty about functional implications.

Minimal overlap on C94-C95. OpenEval accepts these as appropriately cited prior literature providing comparative framework. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating on interpretive conclusions suggests these literature citations are accepted but their application to current interpretations may be viewed as incomplete.

Minimal overlap on C96. OpenEval finds observing compact forms in native lysate validates biological relevance of conformational heterogeneity. Peer reviewers do not explicitly address this claim but their UNCERTAIN rating on biological significance interpretations suggests this validation may be viewed as insufficient for full mechanistic conclusions.
